All the save-time edge behaviors work. Open http://maker:4001/edge-save.html and let's walk through the tricky moments. There are two here that are genuinely **your call**, not just a yes/no.

**Please try these:**

1. **Something that isn't a link.** Type `notalink` (no dot) and press Save. → It refuses to save and explains why, rather than creating a broken bookmark. Simple confirm: is a gentle inline message the right response?

2. **A link you already saved** — *your call.* Type `longreads.com/field-guide` (already in your list) and press Save. → I chose to **not create a duplicate**, and instead tell you "you've already saved this" with a **"Show the one you saved"** link that jumps to it. Is that the behavior you want when you re-save something? (The alternative would be to save it twice, or to silently update the existing one.)

3. **A page whose details can't be read** — *your call on the fallback.* Type `broken.example/x` (I've wired that address to simulate a page that gives back no title, description, or image) and press Save. → It **still saves** so you don't lose the link, showing the **address as the title** and "No description could be read." Is "save it anyway with a bare fallback" right, or would you rather it warn you / let you type a title yourself?

4. **Very long text and lots of tags.** Scroll to the top item ("A Comprehensive, Exhaustive…"). I made it deliberately extreme — a huge title, a long description, and ten tags. Check that it stays readable and doesn't break the layout. → Should very long titles/descriptions **wrap and show in full** like this, or would you prefer them **shortened with a "…"** so every card stays compact?

Take your time — tell me your preference on 2, 3, and 4 especially.
